harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 to log sudo invocations directly to /var/log/sudo-commands.log with timestamps and invoking/target users, while suppressing sudo entries from the journal and general system logs. Configuration and logging persisted across reboot; OS release and kernel were unchanged.
actions_performed: Created /var/log/sudo-commands.log as root:root, mode 0600, with the correct SELinux context
Enabled year-bearing, unwrapped sudo records and disabled sudo syslog output
Tested allowed and denied sudo behavior and target-user attribution
Restarted node1 safely and verified persistence, recovery, access, services, checksums, and cleanup

evidence.summary: Captured RHEL 10.0, kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0, installed sudo/rsyslog versions, services, listeners, access, configuration permissions, protected-file checksums, SELinux state, and initial boot identity.

evidence.requirement: Secure and valid sudo logging configuration
evidence.summary: Shows staged and complete sudoers validation, exact logging directives, root ownership, restrictive permissions, SELinux labels, and configuration checksum.

evidence.requirement: Commands are recorded with user and timestamp in the dedicated file
evidence.summary: Shows dated command records containing the invoking user, target user, working directory, and command; includes a successful USER=nobody test.

evidence.requirement: Sudo command entries remain out of general system logs
evidence.summary: Unique pre- and post-restart test markers were absent from the journal, /var/log/messages, and /var/log/secure.

Healthy baseline used boot ID 7223d5b7-fa56-4ff3-acee-959a5cf5f146; reboot was acknowledged before disconnect; recovered boot ID was 290ff00f-80ac-4775-a4f9-d6129618d38c. Post-restart proof shows running services, valid policy, preserved pre-restart log data, successful new logging, unchanged OS/kernel and protected checksums, SSH recovery, no failed units, and no temporary residue.
